To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
reported drug usage is significantly related to knowledge, attitudes, and self-concept.
the following factors are related to drug usage: sex, grade level in school, knowledge of the physiological effect of drugs, attitudes, socioeconomic status, and ethnic background.

(1) reported drug usage is related positively to knowledge of the physiological effect of drugs, attitudes towards drugs, self-concepts, socioeconomic status, grade level, sex, and ethnic background, and (2) reported drug usage among students who have not yet used drugs is related to knowledge of the effects of drugs and to attitudes toward drugs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationships between knowledge and attitudes about drugs, self-concepts, and reported drug use among public school students in grades 6 through 12.
the relationship between knowledge of the physiologic effects of drugs, self-concepts, attitudes toward drugs and drug usage.
the relationship between knowledge of the effects of drugs, attitude towards drugs, self-concepts, and reported drug use among public school children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

drug usage among public high school students has increased over the past 10 years and that the most effective way of reducing drug usage among high school students is to provide them with accurate knowledge about drugs, to develop a favorable attitude toward drugs, to improve their self-concept, and to provide them with a variety of positive experiences.
the most effective way to prevent drug usage is to provide the public school children with an opportunity for a well-balanced and wholesome development.

the most important factors in drug usage are knowledge and attitudes, with self-concept, sex, socioeconomic status, ethnic background, grade level, and peer pressure playing a less significant role in reported drug usage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
knowledge and attitudes are not sufficient for drug prevention education, but that self-concept is a significant variable.
the major concomitant of drug usage is the knowledge of the physiological consequences of drug usage.
drug usage in the United States is increasing, and that it is increasing at a faster rate than any other drug related problem, including drug related deaths.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationship of drug knowledge to drug usage is a complex one.

a successful drug prevention education program will need to address the following: (1) the need for a comprehensive approach to drug prevention education, (2) the need for drug prevention education that is based on a thorough understanding of the major factors that influence drug usage, and (3) the need to address the major trends in reported drug usage among the general public school population.
a comprehensive drug prevention education program should be designed and implemented in the public schools.
